definition_en: very pleasing to the senses or to the mind
core_image: 夕阳穿过窗子，把整间屋子的轮廓都镀上一层暖金
scene: 雨停了，山谷里的水面把云影完整地映出来。 The valley looked beautiful after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 beautiful 是「外貌美丽」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她穿了一条美丽的裙子。

senses.title: Pleasing to look at or hear
senses.definition: very pleasing to the eyes or ears
senses.definitionCN: 看起来或听起来非常悦目悦耳的
senses.example: The garden looks beautiful in spring.
senses.why: Beautiful is beauty plus the suffix -ful, so its first job is to describe something full of beauty, whether a face, a view or a song.
senses.whyCN: beautiful 是 beauty 加后缀 -ful，最初的意思就是「充满美的」，所以首先用来形容容貌、景色或歌声。

senses.title: Excellent or very well done
senses.definition: very good or impressive, used in praise
senses.definitionCN: 非常好、令人赞叹，用于称赞
senses.example: What a beautiful goal!
senses.why: Speakers borrowed the word from looks to performance: a beautiful goal or a beautiful pass is not pretty but perfectly executed.
senses.whyCN: 说话的人把这个词从「外表」挪到「表现」：a beautiful goal 或 a beautiful pass 不是好看，而是完成得极为漂亮。

intro.cn: beautiful 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Latin bellus meant 'pretty, fine', a small-scale word of praise.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 意为「好看、精致」，是一个程度较轻的赞美词。

items.en: Old French beau and belle carried the Latin word into French.
items.cn: 古法语 beau 与 belle 把这一拉丁词带入法语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed beaute, the noun for beauty.
items.cn: 中古英语借入名词 beaute，即「美」。

items.en: Beautiful was formed in English from beauty plus the suffix -ful.
items.cn: beautiful 是在英语中用 beauty 加后缀 -ful 构成的。

items.en: The adjective widened from looks to sound, character and skill.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个形容词从外貌扩展到声音、品格与技艺。

definition_en: a movable panel that opens and closes an entrance
core_image: 一块木板装在门框上，推开就看见里面的一整个房间
scene: 楼道尽头的那扇木门半掩着，里面透出一条灯光。 He knocked twice and the door opened.

senses.title: A panel that opens an entrance
senses.definition: a movable panel that opens and closes an entrance
senses.definitionCN: 可以开合、用于进出的一道板状物
senses.example: Please close the door.
senses.why: Door comes from Old English duru, the Germanic word for the opening of a house, and the panel sense grew from it.
senses.whyCN: door 来自古英语 duru，是日耳曼语中表示房屋开口的词，能开合的门板义项由此发展而来。

senses.title: The entrance or doorway itself
senses.definition: the opening or space where you enter
senses.definitionCN: 供人进出的开口或位置
senses.example: Someone is standing at the door.
senses.why: People say at the door when they mean the opening rather than the panel, so the word names both the thing and the space.
senses.whyCN: 人们说 at the door 时指的是开口而不是门板，所以这个词既指门板也指门口的空间。

senses.title: A way to reach an opportunity
senses.definition: a means of reaching an opportunity or a new situation
senses.definitionCN: 通向机会或新境况的途径
senses.example: Education opens doors for young people.
senses.exampleCN: 教育为年轻人打开机会之门。

senses.whyCN: 真实的门让人进入房间，英语用同一幅画面比喻任何能让人进入新机会的东西。

definition_en: a public show of works or objects, or a display of a quality
core_image: 美术馆的长厅里挂满画作，人们沿着墙慢慢看
scene: 美术馆的长厅里挂满画作，人们沿着墙慢慢看。 We visited the art exhibition on Sunday.

senses.title: A public show
senses.definition: a public show of works or objects
senses.definitionCN: 公开展出作品或物品的活动
senses.example: We visited the art exhibition on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们星期天去看了那场美术展。
senses.why: From Latin exhibeo 'hold out, present', through French; the noun names the organised event where things are held out to view.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 exhibeo「伸出、呈现」，经法语进入英语；这个词指把东西伸出来给人看的活动。

senses.title: The act of showing
senses.definition: the act of showing something to the public
senses.definitionCN: 把某物公开展出的行为
senses.example: The exhibition of the new car drew crowds.
senses.why: The same noun can name the showing itself rather than the event, as when a single object is put on display.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可以指展示这个行为本身而不是整场活动，比如把单件物品摆出来给人看。

senses.title: A display of a quality
senses.definition: a display of a skill, quality or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 技能、品质或情感的显露
senses.example: His calm was a fine exhibition of courage.
senses.exampleCN: 他的镇定是勇气的出色表现。
senses.why: Because showing is the core idea, the word extends to any visible display of a quality, not only objects in a hall.
senses.whyCN: 因为「展示」是核心意思，这个词也扩展到任何看得见的品质流露，而不只是展厅里的物件。

definition_en: the day of the week after Monday and before Wednesday
core_image: 一周的第二天，脚步已经走顺
scene: 每个星期二下午，我们都有游泳课。 Every Tuesday afternoon, we have a swimming lesson.

senses.exampleCN: 星期二比星期一安静些。
senses.why: The day is named after the god of war, yet in the week it simply takes the second step.
senses.whyCN: 这一天以战神命名，但在一周里它只是迈出第二步。

senses.title: An ordinary working day
senses.definition: a weekday seen as an ordinary day of work or school

senses.example: Tuesday feels like a normal school day.
senses.exampleCN: 星期二感觉就是平常的上学日。
senses.why: Once the week has started, the second day settles into routine, so the name can stand for an ordinary weekday.
senses.whyCN: 一周既已开始，第二天就落入常规，于是这个名字可以代表普通的工作日。

senses.title: Every Tuesday
senses.definition: used in the plural for something that happens each Tuesday
senses.definitionCN: 用复数表示每逢星期二发生的事
senses.example: Tuesdays are my busiest days.
senses.exampleCN: 星期二是我最忙的日子。
senses.why: The repeated day becomes a pattern, so the plural names the habit rather than a single date.
senses.whyCN: 重复的一天变成规律，于是复数命名的是习惯而不是某个日期。

definition_en: to shut something, to end, or to be near in space or time
core_image: 两扇门慢慢合拢，最后一道缝也消失了
scene: 傍晚的店里客人渐渐走空，店主走到门口准备收工。 She closed the shop and turned off the lights.

senses.title: To shut something
senses.definition: to shut a door, window or lid
senses.example: Please close the window.
senses.why: The verb close comes from Latin claudere, to shut, and the physical act of shutting is its oldest use.
senses.whyCN: 动词 close 来自拉丁语 claudere「关闭」，把东西合上这个具体动作是最早的用法。

senses.title: To bring something to an end
senses.definition: to end an activity, meeting or period
senses.definitionCN: 使活动、会议或时期结束
senses.example: The shop will close at six.
senses.why: Shutting a building or a meeting is like shutting a lid: activity stops, so close also means to end.
senses.whyCN: 关上一栋楼或一场会议就像盖上盖子：活动停止，所以 close 也表示「结束」。

senses.title: Near in space or time
senses.definition: near in distance or time
senses.example: We live close to the school.
senses.why: This adjective is pronounced with a soft s and comes from French clos, enclosed, meaning places packed near one another.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词读作清音 s，来自法语 clos「围起来的」，指彼此挨得很近的地方。

senses.title: Near in relationship
senses.definition: having a strong personal bond
senses.example: We are close friends.
senses.why: People who live close become emotionally close, so the distance word extends to relationships.
senses.whyCN: 住得近的人感情也会近，于是表示距离的词扩展到了关系上。

senses.title: The end part of the leg
senses.definition: the part of the body at the end of the leg, used for standing and walking
senses.definitionCN: 腿的末端，用来站立和行走
senses.example: He hurt his foot on the rocks.
senses.why: Foot goes back to Old English fōt and shares its root with Latin pēs, the word for the walking end of the leg.
senses.whyCN: foot 来自古英语 fōt，与拉丁语 pēs 同源，指腿末端用来行走的部分。

senses.title: A unit of length of twelve inches
senses.definition: a unit of length equal to twelve inches
senses.definitionCN: 等于十二英寸的长度单位
senses.example: The table is three feet long.
senses.why: The foot was the first ruler people had, so its length became a standard unit of measurement.
senses.whyCN: 脚是人最早随身带的尺子，它的长度因此成了标准的长度单位。

senses.title: The bottom or base of something
senses.definition: the lowest part of something, such as a hill or a page
senses.definitionCN: 山、书页等事物最下面的部分
senses.example: The village lies at the foot of the hill.
senses.why: A foot bears a body from below, so the lowest part that supports a thing is also called its foot.
senses.whyCN: 脚从下面托住身体，所以支撑事物的最下段也被叫作 foot。

senses.title: To pay a bill
senses.definition: to pay the cost of something, in the phrase foot the bill
senses.definitionCN: 在 foot the bill 中承担费用
senses.example: Who will foot the bill for the trip?
senses.why: In the fixed phrase foot the bill, foot works as a verb meaning to settle the cost, as if the payer stood at the bottom of the account.
senses.whyCN: 在固定短语 foot the bill 里，foot 作动词表示结清费用，好像付钱的人站在账单的最下面。

core_image: 操场上孩子们追着足球跑，笑声传得很远
scene: 操场上孩子们追着足球跑，笑声传得很远 Children chase a football across the playground, and the sport fills the air with laughter.

senses.title: A game or activity with physical effort
senses.definition: A game or activity with physical effort

senses.example: Swimming is my favourite sport.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳是我最喜欢的运动。

senses.whyCN: 古法语 desport 意为消遣，英语缩短这个词，保留玩闹用力的意思。

senses.why: The singular without an article names the whole field, not one game.
senses.whyCN: 不带冠词的单数指整个领域，而非某一项比赛。

senses.title: To wear something proudly
senses.definition: To wear something proudly
senses.example: He sported a bright new cap.
senses.exampleCN: 他得意地戴着一顶鲜艳的新帽子。

definition_en: the country in North America

scene: 地图上北边那片土地，枫叶标志贴在最上面。 Her cousin lives in Canada.

senses.title: The country in the north of North America
senses.definition: the country occupying the northern part of North America
senses.definitionCN: 占据北美洲北部的国家
senses.example: Her cousin lives in Canada.
senses.why: Canada comes from kanata, a word in the language of the St Lawrence peoples meaning 'village'; French explorers took it for the name of the whole land.
senses.whyCN: Canada 来自圣劳伦斯河一带原住民语中的 kanata「村落」，法国探险家误把它当作整片土地的名字。

senses.title: Used in names of plants and animals of that region
senses.titleCN: 加拿大的（用于动植物名）
senses.definition: placed before the name of a species associated with Canada, as in Canada goose
senses.definitionCN: 放在物种名前，表示与加拿大有关，如 Canada goose
senses.example: A Canada goose landed on the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 一只加拿大雁落在池塘上。
senses.why: Some species are so closely tied to that country that its name became part of their everyday name, as with the Canada goose.
senses.whyCN: 有些物种与这个国家关系密切，国名就成了它们日常名称的一部分，比如加拿大雁。
